The window, the frame rate and the graphics.

How the game takes the screen. Fullscreen sets the display to the game's resolution. Borderless covers it with a window that others open over. Windowed is a window to move and resize. F11 switches between the two.
What fullscreen and borderless draw at. Native is the display's own, the sharpest; a lower one is lighter on a slow computer, and softer. Fullscreen sets the display to it; borderless scales it.
The window's size: 4:3 first, then 16:10, 16:9 and 21:9. Its edges can also be dragged.
How many times a second the display shows a picture while the game is fullscreen. Auto keeps the display's own. VSync and Max FPS's Auto follow it.
VSync, variable refresh (G-SYNC, FreeSync), the most frames a second and low latency.

How wide you see on foot, in degrees across 16:9. Default is the Xbox's. Above 150 needs Panini Projection. Passengers use it too; driver and gunner: First Person.|Click the number (or press A) to type 20 to 160. Capped at 110 in Pro 2v2 games.
Which way up you hold the device. Portrait has a strip of buttons along the top, the picture under it and the touch controls below it. Auto turns with the device.
Where the picture sits on a screen taller than it, its shape, and the frame around it in portrait.
The vehicles' and scopes' fields of view, the Panini projection, how far you see, the reticle, a passenger's view, and your weapon, body and shields.

Plays the Xbox's intro movie as the game starts, and its attract movies on an idle main menu. Any button skips the intro.|They are the bink folder of your Xbox disc image, copied with the maps. Without them, put the disc's bink folder beside your maps folder.
Enhanced: smoother edges, sharper textures and shadows, smoother lighting. Classic looks as the Xbox did.|Changing one shows CUSTOM.
Draws text and titles with sharp high-resolution fonts. Off draws the game's own.
Up to 60 frames a second and Classic graphics, for a longer battery and a cooler device. Auto turns it on while the device runs on its battery. Your own settings come back as it turns off.
How bright the picture is: its gamma, and on an HDR display, HDR's look, how bright white and the HUD are, and the display's peak.
Render resolution, anti-aliasing, texture filtering, model detail, shadows, the lighting and the shields' glow, smooth motion and the tick rate.
